name: Walter
bio: A youth whom Wilde, writing to Robert Ross in January 1899, named as the object of I. D. W. Ashton's 'absurd love' - the one thing about Ashton he could not forgive. Wilde describes him as 'a plain, crooked, ugly, and tedious youth'. Nothing else is recorded: no surname, no age, no occupation, no trace beyond the single sentence.
bio_note: THE RECORD PRESERVES A FIRST NAME ONLY, and one sentence with it. Sole source: Wilde to Robert Ross, Thursday [? 12 January 1899], Hotel des Bains, Napoule, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1118 - the editors' own query mark on the date is preserved. Transcription and provenance reused unchanged from the context_engagement on ashton.json, where this was held off-roster until 2026-08-05. Wilde's description of him is unkind and is recorded as Wilde's, not endorsed; it is also the only physical description of any kind that survives of this man.
